summary: Defines an RTCP Extended Report block with two new segment types and SDP parameters that allow the reporting of Mean Opinion Score (MOS) metrics for RTP applications.

eli5.summary: After a phone call, people can rate the sound from one to five. This lets software report that kind of score automatically.

subtitle: A way for RTP endpoints to report how good the audio or video sounded or looked, as a mean opinion score.

tldr.problem: Packet loss, delay and jitter alone do not tell you how good a call or video really looked or sounded, because codecs and application behavior also affect quality.
tldr.mechanism: A new RTCP Extended Report block (type 29) carries MOS values in per-stream or per-channel segments, and a new SDP attribute maps a short ID in each segment to the algorithm that computed it.
tldr.outcome: Endpoints and monitors can exchange algorithm-based quality scores for RTP sessions in a standard way, with a new IANA registry for the calculation algorithms.

today: RFC 7266 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no obsoleting or updating RFC. It extends the RTCP Extended Report framework of RFC 3611.

sections.title: Why Report a MOS
sections.content:
RFC 7266 defines a new block for RTCP Extended Reports (RFC 3611), used with RFC 3550, that reports media quality using standard metrics such as the mean opinion score (MOS). It follows the Performance Metrics Framework (RFC 6390) and the guidelines in RFC 6792, and belongs to the class of application-level metrics defined there.

The RFC splits the factors that affect quality in two. Transport factors are packet loss, delay and jitter. Content and codec factors include codec type, loss recovery technique, coding bit rate and packetization. Transport factors alone may not predict quality, so quality can be measured by comparing input and output streams, or estimated by algorithms that model the interaction.

Uses listed include detecting delivery or encoding problems, tuning the encoder, choosing techniques as conditions change, and prequalifying a network.
sections.eli5: A bumpy road does not tell you how sick you felt in the car. This report tells you how the ride actually felt, not just how bumpy the road was.

sections.title: What the MOS Means Here
sections.content:
A MOS is usually on a scale from 1 to 5, where 5 is excellent and 1 is unacceptable, though other ranges such as 0 to 10 or 0 to 100 are possible. The term comes from subjective testing, where it is the mean of individual opinion scores. Here the scores come from objective or estimation algorithms, which allow much larger scale measurement. ITU-T and ITU-R recommendations are cited as defining such methods, and the RFC suggests using them where they exist.

The block reports quality of the received media stream, typically measured at the receiving end. It does not include factors outside the RTP stream, such as signaling performance. It refers by SSRC to the Measurement Information block (RFC 6776) for the measurement period. Senders MUST send it in the same compound RTCP packet as that block, and receivers MUST discard the MOS block if the measurement period did not arrive in the same packet.
sections.eli5: It is like a teacher giving the sound a grade. A computer guesses the grade, using a formula, instead of asking people one by one.

sections.title: The MOS Metrics Block
sections.content:
The block starts with BT=29, a 2-bit interval flag I, 6 reserved bits and a 16-bit block length, then the 32-bit SSRC of the source, then one or more 32-bit segments. The interval flag is 10 for interval, 11 for cumulative and 01 for sampled. A sampled value MUST NOT be sent and MUST be discarded when received. Reserved bits MUST be zero and are ignored by receivers.

Each segment starts with a type bit. Zero means a single-channel segment (one media stream per RTP stream, identified by SSRC); one means a multi-channel audio segment. The two types cannot be mixed in one block. Both carry an 8-bit CAID (calculation algorithm ID) and a 7-bit payload type. The single-channel MOS value is 16 bits in 7:9 fixed point; the multi-channel segment has a 3-bit channel identifier and a 13-bit MOS value in 7:6 fixed point.

Reserved values mark special cases. In the 16-bit value, 0xFFFE means out of range and 0xFFFF means unavailable. In the 13-bit value, they are 0x1FFE and 0x1FFF. Other values outside the algorithm's range MUST NOT be sent and MUST be ignored. If the payload type changes during a session, separate reports SHOULD be sent for each payload type.
sections.eli5: The report is a small form. The top says what kind of form it is, and then each box inside holds one score, which algorithm made it, and which sound channel it is for.

sections.title: Signaling Algorithms in SDP
sections.content:
The CAID in each segment is only a session-specific number. SDP maps it to an algorithm name. The RFC extends the rtcp-xr attribute from RFC 3611 with an xr-format value, mos-metric, whose entries use the new calgextmap element. The form is calg:<id>, an optional direction, then an algorithm name such as G107 or P1202_1. Valid IDs are 1 to 255; 0 can indicate a rejected algorithm. Each ID MUST be unique and used once per stream or channel, and the mapping MUST be given per media stream.

An optional mosref says whether the MOS is for lower (l), middle (m) or higher (h) media resolution, because narrowband and wideband codecs, or SD and HD video, use the same numeric range but SHOULD report different values.

In offer/answer, IDs 4096 to 4351 are an unusable range used for offering alternatives or more entries than fit. The answerer picks what it wants and remaps it to a free ID in the valid range. To reject a mosref value, the answerer uses an ID in 4096 to 4351 and the answer MUST contain the offered mosref value. XR blocks MAY also be used without prior signaling.
sections.eli5: The two sides first agree on nicknames: "when I say number 1, I mean grading method G107." After that the reports can use the short nickname.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
IANA assigned block type 29 to the MOS Metrics Block, registered the mos-metric parameter in the RTCP XR SDP parameters registry, and recorded the calgextmap SDP attribute (media or session level). The RFC also creates a new registry, "RTCP XR MOS Metric block - multimedia application Calculation Algorithm", under the RTCP XR block type registry. The policy is Specification Required, and a registration needs an unambiguous definition of the metric.

Initial entries include P564, G107, TS101_329, JJ201_1, G107_1, P862, P862_2, P863, P1201_1, P1201_2, P1202_1 and P1202_2. Each has a type of voice, multimedia or video.
sections.eli5: There is now an official list of grading methods, with a name for each, and new methods can be added if they are clearly described.

sections.title: Security
sections.content: The RFC says the new blocks introduce no new security considerations beyond those in RFC 3611.
sections.eli5: The new report does not add any new safety worries beyond the ones that already come with the old kind of report.

fields.name: BT=29
fields.desc: Block type for the MOS Metrics Block.

fields.name: I
fields.desc: Interval flag: 10 interval, 11 cumulative, 01 sampled (not to be sent).

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: Set to zero and ignored by the receiver.

fields.name: Block Length
fields.desc: Block length in 32-bit words, minus one.

fields.name: SSRC of source
fields.desc: As defined in Section 4.1 of RFC 3611.

fields.name: CAID
fields.desc: Session-specific reference to the calculation algorithm signaled in SDP.

fields.name: PT
fields.desc: RTP payload type in use during the reporting interval.

fields.name: MOS Value
fields.desc: Unsigned 7:9 fixed point; 0xFFFE out of range, 0xFFFF unavailable.

fields.name: S
fields.desc: Segment type; one for multi-channel audio.

fields.name: CAID
fields.desc: Session-specific reference to the calculation algorithm signaled in SDP.

fields.name: PT
fields.desc: RTP payload type, as in the single-channel segment.

fields.name: CHID
fields.desc: Identifies the audio channel within the RTP stream.

fields.name: MOS Value
fields.desc: Unsigned 7:6 fixed point; 0x1FFE out of range, 0x1FFF unavailable.
